title: Check If N and Its Double Exist

analysis.problem_summary: Determine if an integer array contains two distinct elements where one is exactly twice the value of the other.
analysis.intuition: To check for a target arithmetic relation between pairs without performing an $O(n^2)$ double loop, we can store previously visited numbers in a hash set. For each number `num`, it could represent either the smaller half ($arr[j]$) or the larger double ($arr[i]$) of a valid pair. Therefore, we check if either its double (`2 * num`) or—if `num` is even—its half (`num / 2`) already exists in our set. Checking before inserting `num` into the set automatically ensures that the two elements come from distinct indices, even when handling zero.
approach: Initialize an empty hash set `set` to store integers visited during iteration.
Iterate through each element `num` in the array `arr`.
Check if `set` already contains `2 * num`, indicating `num` is the half-value of a previously seen number.
Check if `num` is even (`num % 2 == 0`) and `set` contains `num / 2`, indicating `num` is the double of a previously seen number.
If either condition is true, immediately return `true`.
Add `num` to `set` for future element checks.
If the loop finishes without finding any valid pair, return `false`.
analysis.why_it_works: Any valid pair of indices $(i, j)$ with $arr[i] = 2 	imes arr[j]$ has one element appearing earlier in the array than the other. By checking both `2 * num` and `num / 2` against previously stored elements before adding the current element to the set, the algorithm guarantees detection regardless of whether the double or the half appears first, while strictly enforcing $i \neq j$.
analysis.time_explanation: The array of length $n$ is traversed once, and each hash set lookup and insertion takes $O(1)$ time on average.
analysis.space_explanation: In the worst case, the hash set stores up to $n$ unique elements when no valid double pair exists.
analysis.key_takeaway: When searching for asymmetric pairwise relationships in an unsourced array, a single-pass hash set checking both possible directional conditions ($2 \times x$ and $x / 2$) achieves optimal linear time while enforcing distinct indices.
